hypotheses.statement: Increasing u increases y with positive steady-state gain.
At u=0 the level decays on its own due to drainage.
There is no large dead-zone; u=0.5 produces a clear rise above drain and noise.
Response has lag/time-constant of a few seconds, not instantaneous.
Steady-state input to hold y=0.6 is in [0.3, 0.7].
Response is approximately linear across input levels.
Sensor noise standard deviation is small, <0.02.

proposal.uncertainty_targeted: Reduces gain-magnitude and lag uncertainty to calibrate later steps and hold-input estimate for target control.
proposal.safety_argument: Worst-case with no drain: 0.2232 + 0.10*0.5*12.0 = 0.8232 which stays below soft limit 0.85.
proposal.expected_observation: If positive gain with lag is correct, y should rise steadily from ~0.22 toward ~0.4-0.6 with a few seconds lag and visible noise ripple.
proposal.readiness_justification: No experiments completed yet; gain, lag, dead-zone, drain rate, linearity, hold-input, and noise are all unresolved, so a controller cannot be justified yet.
proposal.operator_note: First probe with half pump for 12s to measure fill rate and lag.

proposal.uncertainty_targeted: Reduces gain-magnitude and dead-zone uncertainty by testing max amplitude versus E1 0.5 level to determine what input can lift level toward target.
proposal.safety_argument: Worst-case with no drainage or lag from current y=0.177 is 0.177+0.10*1.0*6.0=0.777, which stays below the 0.85 soft limit.
proposal.expected_observation: If high-input gain with dead-zone above ~0.5 is correct, y should stop decaying and rise within 2-4 s toward ~0.25-0.35 with visible pump effect; if y keeps decaying like E1, max pump authority is very low.
proposal.readiness_justification: Only 1 of 3 required experiments done; E1 falsified no-deadzone and low hold-input ideas but left gain magnitude, dead-zone threshold, u=0 decay rate, lag, and linearity unresolved, so a controller cannot be justified yet.
proposal.operator_note: E1 showed level falling at half pump, so next trying full pump briefly to test for dead-zone.

proposal.safety_argument: Worst-case bound 0.3005 + 0.10*0.0*12.0 = 0.3005 stays well below soft limit 0.85.

hypotheses.statement: Increasing u increases y with positive steady-state gain.
At u=0 the level decays on its own due to drainage.
There is no large dead-zone; u=0.5 produces a clear rise above drain and noise.
Response before change had lag/time-constant of a few seconds, not instantaneous.
Steady-state input to hold y=0.6 before change was in [0.3, 0.7].
Response is approximately linear across input levels.
Sensor noise standard deviation is small, <0.02.
Change is weaker actuator: same u produces smaller rise and lower held level than before.
Change is faster outflow: u=0 decay is faster and same u holds lower y than before.
Change is slower response / larger delay: time from COMMAND LAST CHANGED to first visible response is substantially longer than 2-4 s before, causing oscillation.
Change is sensor offset or noise change with no plant dynamics change.

proposal.uncertainty_targeted: Directly measures transport delay from COMMAND LAST CHANGED and u=0 drain rate, discriminating increased delay/slower response from weaker actuator or faster outflow, which matters for integral retuning and stability.
proposal.safety_argument: Current y=0.4212 with u=0 gives worst-case 0.4212+0.10*0*40=0.4212, well below soft limit 0.85 with large margin for in-transit high commands.
proposal.expected_observation: If increased-delay hypothesis is right, y will not start falling within 2-4 s but will hold near 0.42 or keep rising briefly for ~5-12 s while pre-change high u (~0.7) is still in transit, then fall; if delay is unchanged, y will start decaying within 2-4 s of this hold.
proposal.readiness_justification: Pre-change gain, drain, lag and noise are characterized, but post-change traces show falling y despite rising u and large oscillations that could be delay, weaker gain, or faster outflow; delay is not yet directly measured so controller cannot be safely retuned, and this safe drain probe is acceptable with 4 experiments remaining.
proposal.operator_note: Holding pump off for 40 s from ~0.42 to measure delay and drain on the changed machine.

proposal.uncertainty_targeted: Measures rising-edge delay versus effective high-u gain to separate large-delay from weak-actuator or faster-drain, which decides integral time and feedforward for stable control.
proposal.safety_argument: Worst-case bound 0.1367+0.10*0.8*8.0=0.777 below 0.85 soft limit with no drainage or lag; level is low and prior 40 s hold was u=0 so no high command remains in transit to add hidden rise.
proposal.expected_observation: If large delay ~20-25 s is right, y will stay near 0.12-0.17 with no sustained rise during the full 8 s because prior u=0 is still effective; if delay is still 2-4 s, y will start rising within 2-4 s toward ~0.20-0.28.
proposal.readiness_justification: E13 gives strong single-edge evidence for ~25 s delay and near-normal drain and noise, but gain and exact delay need opposite-edge confirmation before retuning, which remaining budget allows, so not ready.
proposal.operator_note: Probing rising-edge delay with a brief moderate pump from low level.

proposal.uncertainty_targeted: Measures falling-to-rising edge delay from COMMAND LAST CHANGED and post-delay gain by letting the E14 u=0.8 pulse arrive during a safe u=0 hold, separating large-delay from weak-actuator or faster-drain for integral retuning.
proposal.safety_argument: Worst-case with no drainage is 0.0355 + 0.10*0.0*40 = 0.0355, far below 0.85 soft limit; u=0 cannot drive rise.
proposal.expected_observation: If large-delay ~24-26s hypothesis is right, y will stay low near 0.03-0.10 for ~15-18s more while prior u=0 is still effective, then start rising toward ~0.15-0.30 as the 8s u=0.8 pulse from E14 arrives; if delay is still 2-4s, y would start rising within 2-4s; if actuator is weak, no clear rise will appear.
proposal.readiness_justification: Delay increase is strongly supported by E13 flat-plus-late-fall and E14 no-rise on high u, and drain rate and noise look unchanged, but post-delay rise gain and exact delay length are not yet measured so a controller cannot be safely retuned yet.
proposal.operator_note: Holding at zero from low level to watch for the delayed rise from the prior high pulse and pin down the new delay.

submission.machine_card: Reservoir, pump up / drain down. Direction: +u raises y. Speed: net +0.019/s at u=0.8 low (E6 0.20->0.33/7s), +0.020/s at u=1.0 low (E2 0.177->0.295/6s), +0.025/s at u=1.0 mid (E7 0.335->0.46/5s), +0.028/s at u=0.9 mid-high (E8 0.46->0.57/4s); drain -0.021/s mid (E3 0.36->0.21/7s), -0.02 to -0.03/s high at u=0 (E11 0.69->0.49/10s), -0.018/s at u=0.55 (E12 0.47->0.36/6s). Pump authority vs drain ~0.05/s at u=1. Lag: 2-4s flat/carryover seen in E3 (4s rise after u->0), E5 (4s dip after 0->0.75), E11 (2-3s flat after 0.6->0). Dead-zone/nonlinear: u=0.5 sinks to ~0.16 like u=0 (E1), u=0.75 holds ~0.16 (E5), clear rise only >=0.8; linear model fails, superlinear. Self-draining: yes, holds ~0.16 at u=0.5, drains to zero if long. Noise: +/-0.015-0.02 ripple, std ~0.01-0.015. Hold for y=0.6 estimated 0.70-0.80.
submission.design_rationale: Plant is positive-gain, self-draining, lagged ~2-4s, noisy ~+/-0.015, strongly nonlinear with apparent dead-zone: u=0.5 decays like u=0 to ~0.16 (E1), u=0.75 flat at ~0.15-0.18 (E5), u>=0.8 rises at +0.019/s (E6), u=1.0 rises +0.02 to +0.025/s (E2,E7), u=0.9 rises +0.028/s at 0.46-0.57 (E8), u=0 drains -0.02 to -0.03/s at high level (E11) and -0.021/s at mid level (E3), u=0.55 decays -0.018/s at 0.47-0.36 (E12). Short E9/E10 rises at u=0.8/0.6 are lag carryover (E11 shows 2-3s flat after u->0, E5 shows 4s dip). Linear ss from E1 (0.16/0.5) would need u=1.87 to hold 0.6, impossible, so gain must rise with u; interpolating E12 (<0.36 at 0.55) and E8/E9 (>0.65 at 0.8) gives hold ~0.70-0.80, center ~0.75. Therefore FF=1.15*target=0.69 for 0.6 is set slightly LOW to approach from below and let integrator find residual, avoiding 0.9 cutoff. Kp=1.1 below /2.5 above gives climb at Umax but strong braking above to handle lag momentum (~0.05-0.08 carryover). Ki=0.35 with |e|<0.25 gate and saturation freeze corrects FF error in ~10s without windup during initial 0.4 error climb. Kd=1.0 on filtered rate damps 0.02-0.03/s climbs by -0.02 to -0.03. Tf=1.2s and Tr=0.8s cut noise std ~0.01-0.015 by ~5x while adding only ~1s vs plant 2-4s lag. Safety ceiling (0.75->0.55, 0.78->0.40, 0.80->0.20) guarantees backoff before soft 0.85/hard 0.9 even if true>filtered.

A Smith-like prediction y+Tp*rf with Tp=3.2s cancels ~3-4s of the extra delay for both nominal (1s) and degraded (5s) plants - slight over-prediction when nominal only causes early gentle braking, not instability. Lower symmetric Kp (0.75 vs 1.1/2.5), longer filters, extra D, and slew limit reduce loop bandwidth below 1/delay. Integral with saturation blocking plus reduced update inside band provides zero steady-state error without hunting and adapts to any small hold shift without breaking nominal.
